info.name: RouteAssign - Full Automation Collection
info.description:
Complete RouteAssign collection for live API testing.

How to use:
1. Import this file into Postman.
2. Make sure your Spring Boot server is running on http://localhost:8080.
3. Run the folders IN ORDER using the Collection Runner (or Postman AI):
   Phase 1 — Seed: Auth → Items → Stock
   Phase 2 — Orders & Lifecycle
   Phase 3 — Query & Read
   Phase 4 — Edge Cases & Errors

All tokens and IDs are captured automatically via test scripts and stored as collection variables. No manual editing needed.

item.name: Phase 1 — Seed Data
item.description: Run this entire folder first. It registers all users, creates items, and stocks every vendor. All tokens and IDs are saved automatically.

exec: if (j.data && j.data.token) { pm.collectionVariables.set('c1Token', j.data.token); pm.collectionVariables.set('token', j.data.token); }

item.name: 1.2 Auth — Login (save tokens + resolve IDs)
item.description: Logins capture tokens. The GET calls after each login resolve the profile ID (vendorId, partnerId, customerId) from the auth userId returned by login.

item.name: Create Item 6 — Mineral Water Case (8 kg)
1.4 Store — Stock all Vendors

item.name: Phase 2 — Orders & Delivery Lifecycle
item.description: Place 6 orders across 3 vendors and 3 customers. Each order captures the returned assignmentId. Then walk orders 1–3 through full delivery lifecycle. Order 4 is cancelled. Orders 5–6 test busy-partner reuse and capacity edge cases.
